feat(verify): B13 the verifier — npx thetacog-mcp verify <row.json> prints MATCH · MISMATCH · UNVERIFIABLE with the reason: ed25519 over the canonical tuple, the placement recomputed from the commit and the reef blob with the same walk; the clearing primitive a claims engine runs without us

Originating-Terminal: 📐 architect (vscode)

Relevant-Rooms: navigator, architect, vault

Story: Spec §8.50 names B13 as the one thing missing from the double-entry frame — a debit (the signed intent) with no independent credit a stranger can check. This ships that credit-side check as a single command: verify a row's ed25519 signature over its own canonical tuple, and — only once that holds — reproduce the row's placement from the commit and the reef/axes git blobs it names, walked with the same pmu-onchip instrument. The verifier lives at scripts/pmu/verify-row.mjs (bundled into the npm tarball the same way attest.mjs and prove-rice.mjs are, via bundle-pmu.mjs's ENTRIES list and server.js's existing [cmd, rel] dispatch loop — no second dispatcher, no import of the private repo's src/lib/pmu/, every needed function copied and attributed inline) so a claims engine with only the published package and a checkout of the repository can run it standalone. VR-1 through VR-6 sign rows with a throwaway key generated fresh in the test (never the room's host-derived identity), and VR-6 recomputes a real signed commit-reality row captured from this repo's own tape against a real commit and the real pmu-onchip binary, landing MATCH end to end.
